blocking_findings.title: Diagnostic-method results can silently downgrade to legacy shape
blocking_findings.detail: Method selection distinguishes diagnostic-capable runtime from legacy, but result validation does not retain that distinction. A diagnostic method returning a bare five-Boolean dictionary bypasses the envelope branch and is labelled legacy_result/unavailable. With all true it is accepted and query_passed becomes true, despite the diagnostic-capable method omitting its required stage/code envelope. The intended legacy compatibility is for absence of the diagnostic method, not malformed results from that method.
blocking_findings.reproduction: Use existing synthetic running-update harness; add verify_evidence_diagnostic returning dict.fromkeys(KEYS, True), and make verify_evidence raise if called. One diagnostic call occurs, no old-method retry, but query_passed is true, shape_valid true and diagnostic legacy_result/unavailable.
blocking_findings.impact_limit: All-five-true criterion was not bypassed; the production adapter separately rejects bare remote wire results. This is an installer interface/diagnostic-integrity gap and missing negative test, not a demonstrated live evidence-verification exploit.
blocking_findings.required_next_proof: When the selected method is diagnostic-capable, require its strict envelope and reject a bare dictionary. Preserve bare five-Boolean compatibility only on the explicitly selected legacy method. Add both diagnostic-bare refusal and old-caller success tests; do not add retry/fallback.

blocking_findings.title: Duplicate JSON members overwrite failed checks before strict validation
blocking_findings.detail: The remote wire uses plain json.loads, which collapses duplicate keys before diagnostic_result_valid sees the object. A nested content_hash false followed by content_hash true is accepted as all true with complete/ok. Repeated top-level checks/diagnostic objects can likewise overwrite an all-false/rejected envelope with all-true/ok. The advertised closed strict envelope therefore accepts ambiguous malformed wire content. Duplicate rejection on remote INPUT does not protect this output decoder.
blocking_findings.reproduction: Using existing FakeDocker adapter fixture with _command replaced by fixed bytes, return all required checks with content_hash:false then duplicate content_hash:true, plus complete/ok. verify_evidence_diagnostic accepts. Also reproduced duplicate top-level checks and diagnostic where later success replaces earlier failure.
blocking_findings.impact_limit: This is a decoder/boundary contract gap. Plain JSON last-key-wins behavior existed in the earlier adapter parser too; this review is requiring strictness for the newly introduced diagnostic wire, not asserting a newly observed runtime attack. The fixed serializer was not shown to emit duplicates, and no live remote operation was performed.
blocking_findings.required_next_proof: Reject duplicate JSON keys at every object depth before envelope validation, with tests for duplicate top-level checks/diagnostic and nested Boolean/stage/code members. Retain one command, same bounds and fail-closed behavior.

shown_preservation.timer_and_teardown: Remote eight-second hard exit uses only precomputed deadline bytes and hard exits including teardown. Occupied timer refuses without modification. Ordinary evaluation failure is retained when later teardown errors; deadline reports current interrupted group instead. Successful evaluation followed by teardown/cleanup error becomes failed checks. First group is not exact predicate/value or historical cause.
